source_goals_preserved.instruction: An instrument stand stands on the table: a top plate carrying a bolted instrument, on two telescoping legs (left leg and right leg, 0.3 m apart). Each leg is locked at its height by a pull-knob pin (red knob) through a row of holes 2.5 cm apart in the inner tube. Pulling a knob out frees that leg; letting the knob go returns the pin into the hole it faces, unless the pulled knob is turned a quarter turn, which keeps the pin out until the knob is turned back. The top plate has a handle above each leg. A green block 5 cm tall is on the table. Robot: two Panda arms with parallel grippers; the left arm reaches the knobs, the right arm reaches the plate handles. Each finger squeezes with at most 40 N. Joint torque limits 80 N m on joints 1-4, 12 N m on joints 5-7. Keep the wrist force below 60 N; a wrist force above 80 N for 0.1 s aborts the episode. The plate hand may need a wrist force guard up to about 50 N. Tool workspace for both arms: x from -0.3 to 0.5 m, y from -0.5 to 0.5 m, z from 0.825 to 1.38 m (table top at z = 0.8 m). Hand orientation is commanded as roll/pitch/yaw (rpy_deg, fixed-axis XYZ, as in the bottle task), so a hand can roll about a knob. The instrument is delicate: its acceleration must stay below 3 g and the plate must never move down faster than 0.2 m/s. Goal: raise the stand by two holes on both legs (plate two holes higher than now). Both pins must be back in their holes and the plate level within 3 mm; then let go of everything and keep both hands off the stand for 1 s.
